name: Turkey
research_note: Only 2 of the planned ~8 searches ran before the session-wide WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted. Both confirmed the packet's closed route rather than opening a new one. Statements marked 'background' are prior knowledge, not a snippet.

nso.name: Turkish Statistical Institute (TUIK / Turkiye Istatistik Kurumu)
nso.note: The URL is TUIK's Population Statistics Portal (Nufus Istatistikleri Portali, 'data sources' page), which surfaced; the main site tuik.gov.tr did not surface in a result and is not typed here. The packet already records that MEDAS's 92 subjects include none of the three fields.

latest_census.notes: Turkey stopped enumerating in 2000; since 2007 population comes from the Address-Based Population Registration System (ADNKS) and the 2011 Population and Housing Census was a sample survey (background). Neither asks religion, ethnicity or mother tongue. Snippet evidence: 'The last officially published census covering language data in Turkey was the 1965 census. There were no questions related to the mother tongue or self-identification of people in censuses taken after 1965' (Fanack); 'Turkish census surveys collected questions about mother tongue between 1927-1965. After 1965 ... not asked'; 'Although subsequent censuses may have included questions about mother tongue, the results were not published' (tr.wikipedia 'Turkiye'deki azinliklar' / Cumhuriyet). Ethnicity was never asked directly; mother tongue was the proxy. 1965 national totals: 31,391,421 people; Turkish 28,175,579 (89.76%; another source gives 90.11%); Kurdish (Kurmanji) 2,219,502 (7.07%); Arabic 365,340 (1.16%); Zaza 150,644 (0.48%); Circassian 0.18%; Georgian 0.09%; Laz 0.08%; Pomak 0.07%; Bosnian 0.06%; Albanian 0.04%; Armenian 33,094. Sources note that suppression of Kurdish identity depressed Kurdish declarations.

subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: neither exactly: 67 provinces in 1965 (background) vs 81 admin1 shapes today; the provinces created since 1989 were carved out of 1965 provinces, so most 1965 rows would each cover one to three current shapes. Nothing at ilce (admin2, 972) level.
subnational_sources.evidence: Search summary: 'a Wikipedia reference to the 1965 Turkish census with provincial tables'. Corroborated by the 'Mardin Province' article snippet: 'In the last Turkish census in 1965, Kurdish remained the largest language spoken by 71% of the population in Mardin Province, while Arabic remained the second largest language at 20% and Turkish stood at 8.9%', and by the Commons map 'Mother language in 1965 Turkey census - Kurdish.png', which can only have been drawn from a provincial table. Sixty years old and the project's tier definitions do not contemplate a stale count; flagged as a historical layer, not current composition.

tier_reason: No census since 1965 has asked religion, ethnicity or mother tongue, later mother-tongue collections were never published, and TUIK publishes none of the three (the packet's MEDAS finding stands). The only subnational count is the 1965 mother-tongue table for 67 provinces, which is 60 years old and matches neither current level.
recommended_action: Declare religion, ethnicity and language not_collected at both levels with the reason 'last asked in the 1965 census; not asked or not published since; ADNKS/2011 census carry none' and cite the Fanack and tr.wikipedia snippets. Optional, clearly labelled historical layer: transcribe the 1965 mother-tongue-by-province table from the English Wikipedia '1965 Turkish census' article (67 provinces; needs a 1965-to-current province mapping and a prominent year flag); a runner should confirm the table is actually on the page. Any KONDA or similar survey estimates of Kurdish share by region (not searched) are samples and rank below that.

summary: Turkey is a census-does-not-ask case: mother tongue (and religion) were last asked in the 1965 census, later mother-tongue collections were never published, ethnicity was never asked directly, and the register-based system TUIK has used since 2007 carries none of the three -- which confirms the packet's closed MEDAS route. Both searches that ran agree. The only subnational count is the 1965 mother-tongue table for the 67 provinces of that year, transcribed in the English Wikipedia '1965 Turkish census' article and echoed in province articles (Mardin: Kurdish 71%), which matches neither the 81 current provinces nor the 972 districts and is sixty years old. Tier C: declare all three fields not_collected with the 1965 reason; the 1965 table is an optional, prominently dated historical layer at best.
